market_context: United States/Canada; household dishwasher drying troubleshooting with attention to drying technology, rinse aid, loading, water temperature and faults that need service.
title: Why Is My Dishwasher Not Drying the Dishes?

seo.title: Dishwasher Not Drying? What to Check Before Service
seo.meta_description: Check the cycle, rinse aid, loading, water temperature and drying system. Learn why plastics stay wet and when poor drying points to a real fault.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose a dishwasher that leaves dishes wet and distinguish normal material behavior or settings from a drying-system malfunction.

excerpt: If your dishwasher is not drying well, first confirm the selected cycle includes drying, the rinse-aid dispenser is filled and cups or containers are not trapping water. Plastic usually holds more droplets than glass or ceramic. If the tub finishes cold even with a heated-dry option, error codes appear or drying performance has suddenly changed, service may be needed.
content_html:
Opening the dishwasher and seeing water droplets does not automatically mean the machine has failed. A warm, nearly dry glass, a plastic storage container covered in beads of water and a mug holding a small puddle on its base can all come out of the same cycle for different reasons.

The useful questions are which materials are wet, which cycle was used and whether the tub finishes warm. Those clues usually separate a loading or setting issue from a true drying-system problem.

Start by separating normal moisture from a new loss of drying

Plastic has less thermal mass than glass, porcelain or metal, so it cools quickly and provides less stored heat for evaporation. It is common for plastics to remain wetter. Water that sits in a concave mug base or container lip is also a drainage problem, not proof that the dishwasher failed to dry.

A stronger troubleshooting signal is change: the machine used to dry the same loads well and now everything is soaked, the interior is cold at the end, or a normal drying phase no longer seems to occur.

Check the cycle and options before assuming a component failed

Quick, Eco and energy-saving cycles may use less heat or a different drying strategy. Depending on the model, Heated Dry, Extended Dry, Extra Dry or a similar option may need to be selected when maximum drying is important.

Other machines use condensation drying and do not work like a traditional exposed-heater design. Read the manual before judging one technology by the behavior of another.

Rinse aid is part of drying, not just spot prevention

Rinse aid helps water sheet off surfaces instead of remaining as individual droplets. Whirlpool lists rinse aid among the first checks for poor drying performance.

Make sure the dispenser is not empty and review its dosage setting. If the model allows adjustment, move one step at a time and observe a few cycles rather than immediately turning it to the maximum.

Loading can trap more water than the drying system can remove

Angle cups, bowls and food-storage containers so water can drain. Avoid nesting pieces or blocking circulation. A cup that finishes with a spoonful of water in its base is not something heated air can reliably fix.

Place lightweight plastics where the manufacturer recommends, often on the upper rack, and make sure spray pressure cannot flip them into a position that catches water.

Incoming water temperature can affect the final result

A sufficiently hot final rinse leaves heat stored in dishes, which supports evaporation afterward. Whirlpool cites about 120°F / 49°C incoming water for many models, although the correct specification is the one in your owner's manual.

In homes with a long hot-water run to the kitchen, manufacturers may recommend running the sink briefly until hot before starting the dishwasher. Do not raise the household water-heater setting solely to improve dishwasher drying without considering scald risk and the requirements of your plumbing system.

Do not interrupt the drying phase

Opening the door while the machine is still using heat or controlled condensation releases the temperature it needs to finish. Let the programmed cycle complete.

On the other hand, some dishwashers intentionally open the door near the end to vent humid air. If your model has an automatic-open feature, confirm it is enabled and unobstructed.

A wet inner door does not necessarily mean wet dishes

With condensation-drying systems, moisture may be designed to condense on cooler stainless-steel walls. The door or tub can show droplets while plates and glasses are acceptably dry.

Judge performance by the load and by what is normal for your model, not by a single wet surface.

How can you tell whether the machine is producing heat?

After a cycle that is supposed to use heat, the tub will often feel warm and may release steam when opened. Use caution and do not touch heating components.

If the machine finishes completely cold, also fails to heat wash water, displays an error code or has abruptly lost all drying ability, possible causes include the heater, heat-pump system, fan, vent, sensor or electronic control, depending on the design.

Do not test internal electrical parts with the appliance energized

Checking resistance heaters or internal wiring is no longer a simple household adjustment. If cycle selection, rinse aid, loading and water supply are correct but the machine produces no expected heat, schedule service rather than probing live components.

The sequence that prevents unnecessary parts replacement

Start with the material: if only plastics are damp, the machine may be working normally. Then check the cycle, drying option, rinse aid and loading. Confirm how your specific dishwasher is designed to dry before interpreting a cool tub as a component failure.

The useful question is not simply “are there droplets?” but “is the dishwasher completing the drying process it was designed to use?”

faq.question: Why are plastic containers wetter than glass dishes?
faq.answer: Plastic stores less heat and cools faster, so water evaporates from it less readily than from glass, ceramic or metal.

faq.question: Does rinse aid help dishes dry?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps water sheet and drain off surfaces instead of remaining in beads, improving drying as well as reducing spots.

faq.question: Should the dishwasher feel hot when it finishes?
faq.answer: It depends on the design and selected cycle. If a heated-dry option is selected but the tub consistently finishes cold, check the manual and consider service.

faq.question: Is it normal for the dishwasher door to be wet?
faq.answer: It can be, especially with condensation-drying systems. Evaluate the dishes and the normal behavior of your specific model too.
